title: Bipartite matching is in RP
statement: The language of encodings of bipartite graphs that have a perfect matching belongs to RP under the given verifier model. Explicitly, there are a Boolean verifier $M$ and natural numbers $a,k$ such that the verifier is efficient according to that model, every input word in the language is accepted with probability at least $2/3$ using $a(|x|+1)^k$ uniformly random bits, and every input word outside the language is rejected for every choice of those random bits.
hypotheses_covered: The language is the set of encodings of bipartite graphs with a perfect matching
There exist a Boolean verifier and natural numbers $a,k$
The verifier satisfies the efficiency predicate of the polynomial-time verifier model
For every input word in the language, acceptance probability is at least $2/3$ using $a(|x|+1)^k$ random bits
For every input word outside the language, the verifier rejects for every string of $a(|x|+1)^k$ random bits
